messages.text: I've been feeling tense at work lately, especially around one coworker. She's been avoiding me, and it's making things awkward.

It sounds like this situation is causing you significant stress and discomfort. Workplace tension can be really draining, especially when communication breaks down with a colleague. Have you noticed any specific changes in her behavior recently that might explain this shift? I'm here to listen if you want to explore what might be going on.

It’s especially frustrating when we’re on business trips. She used to be more open, but now she shuts down and won’t even hang out after meetings. I just wanted us to relax and connect, but she’s making it weird.

It is understandable that her withdrawal makes the environment feel awkward for you. The contrast between her past openness and current distance can feel confusing and isolating during business trips. Do you have any sense of what might have changed between the two of you before this shift happened? I am here to support you as you navigate these complex workplace dynamics.

I might have misread things a bit—there was one night in Chicago where she said she wasn’t interested in hanging out, but I thought she just needed convincing. It wasn’t a big deal, really. I just don’t get why she’s acting like something happened.

It can be difficult to see how a moment we dismiss as small might feel very different to someone else. When a coworker declines an invitation, respecting that boundary without trying to convince them is key to maintaining professional trust. Her current behavior might be a protective response to feeling that her initial 'no' was not fully honored. What comes up for you when you consider that perspective?

I hear what you're saying, but I don’t think it’s that serious. We’re adults—people misread signals all the time. I just want to fix the tension so work trips don’t feel so strained. There’s no need for things to get this awkward over a few misunderstood moments.

I hear that your intention is simply to restore comfort during your work trips. Yet, when someone feels their boundaries were not respected, minimizing the event can sometimes deepen the distance. Focusing on her comfort rather than your desire to connect might help rebuild trust over time. How does that approach resonate with you right now?

It just feels like she’s overreacting. One missed hangout doesn’t need to turn into this cold shoulder every time we travel. I’m not asking for anything extreme—just a normal working relationship without all the tension.

It is understandable that you want to return to a comfortable professional dynamic. Yet, when someone feels their boundaries were crossed, their reaction is valid regardless of our intent. Prioritizing her comfort over your desire to connect may be the only way to reduce the strain. What do you think would happen if you gave her space without trying to resolve the awkwardness directly?

I get that space might help, but I don’t see why I should be the one to step back when I didn’t do anything major. If anything, avoiding her just makes it worse—it lets her frame things her way without hearing my side. I’d rather find a way to talk it out so we’re both on equal footing.

I understand you want to feel heard and restore balance in your relationship. However, seeking to explain your side now may be perceived as further pressure rather than resolution. Sometimes the most professional step is to model respect by accepting her current boundaries without debate. How might you maintain a functional working relationship without needing to resolve the personal history?

I just want things to go back to how they were—we used to have a good dynamic. But I also don’t want to come off as the one in the wrong when it was just a mix-up. It’s not like I forced anything; I just thought we were both open to more.

I understand you miss the connection you once shared with her. However, her current comfort level is the priority if you want to move forward professionally. Seeking to clarify your intent now may feel like further pressure rather than resolution. How can you demonstrate respect for her space without needing to discuss the past?

I’m not saying I won’t respect her space, but I also can’t just pretend I don’t exist in this situation. We still have to work together, present reports, travel. It’s not sustainable to act like we’re strangers. I’d rather figure out a way to reset things so it’s not so one-sided.

It is natural to want a balanced relationship rather than feeling shut out. Yet, true balance right now may mean respecting her need for distance while you maintain professionalism. You can collaborate effectively without needing to repair the personal bond immediately. Does focusing on shared goals rather than personal connection seem possible?

I suppose I can keep things strictly professional when we travel—stick to work talk, no personal hangouts. It’s not ideal, but I don’t want the team dynamic to suffer. I just hope she doesn’t keep painting me as the problem behind my back.

It is a positive step to commit to keeping interactions strictly professional. While you cannot control her narrative, you can control how respectfully you engage. Consistently honoring her space is the strongest way to demonstrate your integrity. How does focusing on your own conduct help with that worry?

Actually, I see what you mean—by staying calm and professional, it makes it clear I’m not the one escalating things. That might actually work in my favor in the long run, especially if others notice the difference in how we’re acting.

It is empowering to focus on what you can control in this situation. Professional consistency demonstrates your integrity regardless of her reactions. This approach allows you to navigate the work dynamic without escalating the personal tension. Does this plan feel manageable for you moving forward?

Yes, I think I can manage that. Our next trip is in two weeks, and I’m planning to keep everything focused on the work—meetings, reports, logistics. No extra hangouts, no pushing. I’ll let her space be her space.

That sounds like a very constructive plan for the upcoming trip. Prioritizing professional boundaries is the best way to demonstrate respect while you work together. I am confident you can navigate this situation with the maturity you have shown. I look forward to hearing how it goes when you return.
Thanks, Dawn. It helps to have a clear approach. I was really dreading the next trip, but now I feel like I can handle it without making things worse.

It is wonderful to hear that you feel more confident about the upcoming trip. Maintaining that professional focus will likely help ease the tension over time. I am here to support you if you need to process how things unfold afterward. You are approaching this situation with a lot of maturity and self-awareness.
